key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces by removing excess tin, improving electron extraction and reducing interfacial recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling passivant protonation and surface stoichiometry offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Use neutral ethylenediamine to chelate undercoordinated metals and remove excess surface tin.
Compare with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide, which initially passivates sites before defect-assisted deprotonation.
Use atomistic simulations to examine iodide-vacancy-assisted migration and deprotonation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency, stronger n-type surface character, improved electron extraction into C60, and suppressed interfacial nonradiative recombination.
watch_item: Long-term operational stability and large-area reproducibility are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
